headword: {旅客列車|りょかくれっしゃ}

definitions.explanation: A train that carries passengers, as opposed to one that carries freight. The standard technical term used by railway operators, contrasted with {貨物列車|かもつれっしゃ} (freight train).

examples.japanese: {次|つぎ}に{来|く}るのは{旅客列車|りょかくれっしゃ}です。
examples.english: The next train to arrive is a passenger train.

examples.japanese: この{路線|ろせん}では{旅客列車|りょかくれっしゃ}と{貨物列車|かもつれっしゃ}が{共用|きょうよう}している。
examples.english: Passenger and freight trains share this line.

examples.japanese: {昭和|しょうわ}の{時代|じだい}には、{長距離|ちょうきょり}の{旅客列車|りょかくれっしゃ}に{食堂車|しょくどうしゃ}が{連結|れんけつ}されていた。
examples.english: During the Showa era, long-distance passenger trains had dining cars attached.

notes:
A technical railway term combining {旅客|りょかく} (passenger) and {列車|れっしゃ} (train). Found in timetables, railway announcements, and news about rail accidents. In everyday speech people usually just say {電車|でんしゃ} instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旅客列車|りょかくれっしゃ}が{通過|つうか}する: a passenger train passes through
- {旅客列車|りょかくれっしゃ}の{運行|うんこう}: operation of passenger trains
- {長距離|ちょうきょり}{旅客列車|りょかくれっしゃ}: long-distance passenger train

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {電車|でんしゃ}: train — the everyday word; preferred in conversation
- {貨物列車|かもつれっしゃ}: freight train — the counterpart that carries cargo instead of passengers
- {特急|とっきゅう}{列車|れっしゃ}: limited express train — a type of passenger train that stops only at major stations
